answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a hollow as the anchor of the cost.
